title: SPEC still lists a pin verb the tool dropped six months ago
foundBy: session agent, while reading SPEC 3.1 for the playbook's material

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestSpecNamesEveryCommand -count=1: PASS. Proved by mutation: restoring the old line fails it on two counts, `pin` named with no verb behind it and `playbook` carried by the binary and unnamed. The whole gate is green: make check exit 0, and the surface linter reports 0 errors after the waiver was dropped.

resolution: Section 3.1 lists the verbs the binary has. The dead `pin` is gone, `orientation` and `playbook` are named, and section 7.1 says the upstream check where it used to say pin. The stale `sampleSkip` waiver is dropped from `.cs-lint.yaml`. TestSpecNamesEveryCommand now holds the block against the command tree in both directions, which is the gate this section never had.
details:
SPEC's host command surface lists a `pin` verb that `cs-campaign` does not have.

Section 3.1 prints `cs-campaign doctor|pin|manual|version` as the health and metadata group. Running `cs-campaign pin` answers `unknown command "pin"`, and the root command registers no such verb.

The verb was real and was removed. Commit 133ba66 replaced the operator-written pin file with the `go.mod` embedded in the binary. That change rewrote R75, deleted section 5.8 and dropped the `CS_CAMPAIGN_PIN` variable, and it left the synopsis in 3.1 naming the verb.

Two other traces are left behind. Section 7.1 lists pin among what `internal/cli` holds, which reads as the upstream check rather than a verb and is defensible. `.cs-lint.yaml` carries a `sampleSkip` waiver for `cs-campaign pin --note ...`, and no document contains that sample any more.

The surface linter has the rule that would catch this. SURF-101 refuses a command a document names and the tool lacks, and it reports zero errors here. The line is pipe-separated inside a fenced sh block, which reads as a shell pipeline rather than as four verbs.

SPEC is the contract a reader trusts about the surface. A verb listed there that does not exist is the staleness that makes the rest of the page suspect.

notes.text: The surface linter still cannot read this block. SURF-101 parses `cs-campaign doctor|manual|playbook|version` as a shell pipeline rather than as four verbs, so the rule that exists for this defect stays blind to the synopsis form. The new test covers this repository. Teaching cs-lint the form would cover every project that writes a synopsis this way.

This record was filed as SAC-015 on a branch and renumbered on integration. The maintainer's own SAC-015 reached the remote first, and an ID belongs to whoever integrates it. The record is otherwise unchanged, and the work it describes is unaffected.

The maintainer fixed the same line upstream in a275f4e, which dropped the pin verb and left the section without `orientation`. The merge kept this branch's version, which also names `orientation` and `playbook`. TestSpecNamesEveryCommand is the part that is not duplicated, and it would have caught the missing verb as well as the dead one.
